newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 posts first fall in seven sessions.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 posts first fall in seven sessions.

text.p: The Czech PX50 posted its first decline in seven sessions on Tuesday led by falls from the four most heavily capitalisaed shares on the index.
The PX50 fell 0.5 points, 0.09 percent, to 559.9 and the RPIX lost 1.9 points, 0.16 percent, to 1,161.1
Power utility CEZ, which has surged ahead since the start of 1997 trading on Jan 6, fell back seven crowns to 1,063 on profit taking and fears that its price may have peaked, dealers said.

"Most people realised some profit and they see the price (of CEZ) a little bit high...so maybe they are starting to be worried that the price has reached a peak," said Ivan Kusacek of Zivnostneska Banka in Prague.
SPT Telecom fell 19 crowns to 3,370. Kusacek said it was too early to give reasons for SPT's current downtrend.
In the broader market, brewery Radegast which has surged since Bass Plc announced it had increased its stake in the company to 33 percent, lost 285 crowns to 5,565.
"The price is already high and somebody is trying to pick up every single piece from the market. I would sell it now," said Kusacek.
In the construction sector, the two biggest issues Metrostav and IPS Praha both posted moderate gains.
Overall, turnover was 892 million crowns with volume at 1,064,772 shares.
